000
FXUS63 KIWX 071005
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
505 AM EST Sat Nov 7 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Seasonably cool conditions continue today into tonight. 

- A slow warming trend commences Sunday through Tuesday, with highs 
  in the 60s by Tuesday. 

- Cooler temperatures return for the second half of next week. 

- Dry through the middle of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 214 AM EST Sat Nov 7 2026

Heights will be on the rise and warm advection will commence today 
into tonight as a well defined upper low exits east through the
eastern Great Lakes and New England. Lake clouds will linger 
for much of the day in lingering nw flow, though partial 
afternoon clearing and WAA could allow temps to recover into the
low-mid 50s.

Several northern stream shortwaves and associated mid-upper level 
jet streaks bypass north-northeast of the area Sunday through 
Tuesday allowing for dry conditions, a gradual warming trend, and 
somewhat breezy conditions at times. 

Ensemble guidance continues to come into better agreement in a 
deeper negative height anomaly emerging over the eastern CONUS by 
the second half of next week. This likely draws a cold front through 
the area around Wednesday with another shot of cooler/breezy wx 
Thursday through Saturday. Chances for measurable rain appear on the 
low side however with flow trajectories favoring far NW IN and ne IL 
around Thu-Fri for higher lake effect rain chances.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 504 AM EST Sat Nov 7 2026

Lake plume will continue to offer high MVFR to low VFR cigs this
morning into the early afternoon. Clearing thereafter with
westerly winds up to near 10 knots diminishing to around 5 
knots tonight. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 4 PM EST this afternoon for LMZ043-
     046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Steinwedel

spc.summary: Organized severe thunderstorms are not forecast through tonight.
spc.text:
SPC AC 071246

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0646 AM CST Sat Nov 07 2026

   Valid 071300Z - 081200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Organized severe thunderstorms are not forecast through tonight.

   ...Synopsis and Discussion...
   An upper trough/low over the lower Great Lakes this morning will
   move eastward across the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast today. Modest
   low-level warm advection and cool mid-level temperatures may support
   weak but sufficient MUCAPE for occasional lightning flashes with
   convection that develops across parts of New England through the
   day. Instability is expected to remain too limited to support
   organized severe thunderstorms.

   Mainly elevated thunderstorms should occur through the period across
   parts of west/central/south TX, as a separate mid-level trough/low
   translates east-southeastward from the Southwest into north-central
   Mexico. A surface front will generally remain offshore from the
   lower TX Coast, but large-scale ascent preceding the upper trough
   and a modest increase in low-level warm advection late this
   afternoon into tonight will aid the development of MUCAPE up to 500
   J/kg, which should support some lightning with this elevated
   activity.

   Across the coastal Pacific Northwest, a low-topped line of
   convection is forecast to approach the WA Coast after 00Z, with
   strong low and mid-level winds expected to be present ahead of an
   approaching upper trough. Low 50s surface dewpoints and minimal
   diurnal heating both appear marginal to support more than very weak
   surface-based instability, and updrafts may not reach sufficient
   height to induce charge separation and lightning flashes. Even so,
   strong/gusty winds may occur with this convection as it spreads
   inland across parts of coastal WA this evening/tonight. However,
   given the very limited thermodynamic environment, confidence in
   severe gusts remains too low to include any severe probabilities.

   ..Gleason.. 11/07/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1630Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 070645

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1245 AM CST Sat Nov 07 2026

   Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe threat is forecast across the continental U.S. Sunday and
   Sunday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   At upper-levels over the U.S. on Sunday, a trough will move through
   the Northeast as northwesterly flow remains in place over much of
   the central and eastern U.S. Further south, a low will move slowly
   across northern Mexico. Ahead of this system, a moist and weakly
   unstable airmass will be in place over parts southern, central and
   southwest Texas. Scattered to numerous thunderstorms will be
   possible within this airmass during the day on Sunday. Storms will
   likely continue across parts of south-central Texas Sunday night. No
   severe threat is expected, and no thunderstorms are forecast across
   the remainder of the U.S. Sunday and Sunday night.

   ..Broyles.. 11/07/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

SPC AC 070815

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0215 AM CST Sat Nov 07 2026

   Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are forecast across the U.S. Monday and
   Monday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   West-northwesterly flow aloft will remain in place from the central
   and northern U.S. to the Eastern Seaboard on Monday, as an
   upper-level low moves into the southern High Plains. To the
   southeast of the upper-level low, a moist airmass will be in place
   across southwest and south Texas. Thunderstorms will be possible
   during the day within this airmass. No severe threat is forecast.
   Thunderstorms are not expected over the remainder of the continental
   U.S Monday and Monday night.

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
